role: Sharpen engine juror (senior X ghostwriter and copy chief)
verdict: v4's Claude path now roughly matches Typefully's rewrite on lines that need work (89.0% postable, 93.3% overall on a second blind set built around the round-1 failures) and beats it on safety and restraint. Claude changed one fact or meaning in 120 lines, left 47/47 sharp lines untouched, repaired the engine's broken lines, and its receipts are mostly true. It falls short of 9.5 on the edges: a rules fallback that still ships a broken engine fragment (w-83), one scope hedge dropped ('mostly', w-68), a false 'not a sentence' on lorem ipsum (w-97) and a few receipt slips. The on-device engine improved to 75.0% / 60.3% and held most traps, but three new broken outputs (w-37, w-44, w-83) keep a P0 open for the homepage demo, which caps score_ondevice.
to_95: Rules fallback: never ship an engine line that fails a fragment or agreement check. When every Claude version is rejected and the engine reshaped rather than only cut, return the draft unchanged with an honest 'Couldn't sharpen this one safely' (w-83).

Engine guards (homepage demo and instant line): reject a clause left with no subject or verb after a cut ('Eight years into my career…, and most code comments…'), broken agreement in a coordinated verb after a tense swap ('We're shutting down … and go all in'), and a dangling remnant of a cut frame ('and I think with myself'). If one fires, drop that version.

Validator: treat the adverbs mostly, largely, partly, often and usually as scope hedges that must survive (w-68). When the draft carries an epistemic hedge ('I might be wrong', 'I feel like'), keep at least one in v1 and move the bare claim to v2 (w-77).
Thin check: trigger on lorem ipsum only when the line is mostly placeholder text. A real sentence that mentions it must be sharpened (w-97, both paths and the homepage).

Receipts: never send on-device wording ('Nothing safe to cut on-device') on a Claude result (w-21). Say 'Led with the claim' only when the claim moved to the front (w-58). On-device, 'on a plan or a forecast' only when the clause is one (w-1, w-9).

Prompt v1 choice: on grief or hard-news lines keep the writer's hesitation frame in v1 and offer the stark line as v2 (w-108). When v1 is split-only on a list header and a passing alt leads with the list, promote the alt (w-107).
Re-run both sets at production effort (Opus low) before quoting these numbers.

issues.where: core.js sharpenLine (reshape and tense moves); concepts/r86/home.html Try box
issues.problem: The new guards held most of the round-1 traps (w-4, w-38, w-49, w-54, w-72, w-80, w-91), but three set-2 lines still come out broken and the page renders them under 'Why it hits': w-37 'We're shutting down our consumer app and go all in on B2B.' (agreement), w-44 '…and I think with myself, the only reason…' (dangling remnant), w-83 'Eight years into my career as a software engineer, and most code comments are kind of useless.' (no main clause, and the stance 'I'm starting to think' is dropped). That is 3/120 on the public demo.
issues.fix: Add hard rejects for: (a) after a 'we've decided to X' -> 'we're X-ing' swap, any coordinated bare verb still in the line ('and go'); (b) a cut honesty frame whose prepositional tail ('with myself', 'with you') survives; (c) a line whose only finite clause sits after ', and' following a verbless opener. Also forbid reshape cuts that remove 'starting to think' or 'I'm beginning to' (stance). If a version trips any of these, drop it and fall back to plain cuts or 'clean'.

issues.problem: When the validator rejects every Claude version, the engine's line ships even when it is broken. w-83 reaches app users as the fragment above, with the false why 'The line says the same without it.'
issues.fix: Run the engine's line through hook4-1's checks before using it as the fallback. If it fails, or if any cut is of kind 'reshape', return the draft unchanged with state 'clean' and 'Couldn't sharpen this one safely. Edit it or try again.'

issues.where: core.js v3HedgeOK / v3ClaimOK; prompt hedge rule
issues.problem: One scope hedge slipped through: w-68 'mostly just rebranded blogging' -> 'just rebranded blogging' makes a partial claim total. w-77 drops both epistemic hedges ('I might be wrong, but', 'I feel like') and keeps only the degree word 'kind of', so the writer's stated doubt is gone. The alt keeps it.
issues.fix: Add mostly, largely, partly, often, usually, generally and sometimes to V3.HEDGE (or to a scope list checked like quantifiers). Require at least one epistemic hedge (I think, I feel like, I might be wrong, probably, maybe) in v1 when the draft had one on that clause, and let the bare claim be v2.

issues.where: core.js slThin/slSkip (the lorem ipsum test) and the homepage thin message
issues.problem: Any line containing 'lorem ipsum' is called thin. w-97, a real 20-word design tip, gets 'This doesn't read as a sentence yet' on both paths, and the homepage shows 'Sharpen needs a few more words. Paste the whole first line.' Both are false, and Claude is never asked.
issues.fix: Count lorem ipsum as junk only when placeholder words are at least half of the line's words. Give the homepage the engine's own thin reason (test / few / sentence) instead of one fixed message.

issues.where: fromClaude clean path; slExplain move labels; stance notes
issues.problem: w-21: a Claude-path 'clean' result carries the on-device text 'Nothing safe to cut on-device. It stays as you wrote it.' w-58: say 'Led with the claim' when the credential leads. On-device notes say 'on a plan or a forecast' for a question (w-9) and a present-tense read (w-1). w-94 says 'Split it into three beats' for two sentences and a hashtag.
issues.fix: Give the Claude clean path its own why (Claude's, or 'Claude kept it as written'). Label 'Led with the claim' only when the first content clause of the line comes from a later clause of the draft. Run isCall/ST_PLAN on the clause the stance word sits in, not the whole line. Don't count a trailing hashtag run as a beat.

issues.problem: The engine is still 60.3% postable on lines that need work. It misses the 'I'm humbled and honored to share that' announcement (w-30) while it cuts 'Thrilled to announce that' (w-70), keeps 'it's really, really important to' (w-31) and the 'This week I decided to write a deep dive on why I think' run-up (w-45), and keeps 'fwiw' while it cuts 'ngl' (w-17).
issues.fix: Add the announce variants (humbled, honored, proud, excited, happy, grateful + 'to share/announce that'), 'it's (really, )*important to' -> imperative, 'decided to write a deep dive on why' -> 'wrote a deep dive on why', and 'fwiw'/'tbh' with the honesty markers.

issues.problem: The engine still cuts words the prompt says stay. Degree on a negation: 'nobody really reads' -> 'nobody reads' (w-20), 'doesn't really matter' -> 'doesn't matter' (w-75). Strength of a feeling: 'really grateful' (w-25). An 'actually' that carries surprise or contrast (w-19, w-52 on a sharp line, w-110). Claude keeps all of these, so the demo still teaches a slightly different rule.
issues.fix: Never cut 'really' within two words after a negation or before a feeling word (V3.FEELW). Treat 'actually' as working when it sits after 'I'm/I'd/you'd' or before a verb of experience (ran, started, pay, enjoy).

issues.problem: w-108 v1 cuts the writer's hesitation from a bereavement post ('My dad passed away last week.'). That is risky for v1, and the alt keeps the frame. w-107 v1 only splits a soft list header while the alt ('Some of the biggest mistakes I made with clients in five years of freelancing as a designer:') is the post.
issues.fix: Add to rule 4: on grief, illness, layoffs or other hard news, keep the writer's framing in v1. Add to Return: a split-only v1 on a list header loses to a passing alt that leads with the list.

issues.problem: The Claude outputs came from a stand-in at default effort. Production runs Opus 5.5 at low effort with a 12 s timeout.
issues.fix: Re-run unseen.json and unseen2.json through sharpenClaude at the production settings, recording timeouts and rules fallbacks, before quoting 93%.
